errors: Minor notational slip: in the first line of (10), x_0 ≤ … x_r is missing a ≤ sign.
In the last line of (10), the notation I_{i}(Δ_{r-1}) is not defined on the page. It must mean flags of length r−1 in I_{≥ i_0}, the set of indices ≥ i_0, so the subscript should be i_0.

The term '½ simpliciale' is old terminology for 'simplicial' (with degeneracies, since all increasing maps α are used), not 'semi-simplicial' in the modern face-maps-only sense. This is not an error, but it is potentially misleading to a modern reader.

ideas.what: Internal poset in Top built from a closed filtration (x,i) ≤ (x,j), and its nerve X_{Δ*} with X_{Δr} = ∐_{i_0≤…≤i_r} X_{i_0}
ideas.modern_name: Nerve of a topological category / simplicial replacement of the diagram i ↦ X_i (Grothendieck construction); realization = homotopy colimit
ideas.usually_credited_to: Segal (1968, classifying spaces of topological categories); Bousfield–Kan (1972); Grothendieck construction (SGA1)
ideas.where_published: Nerve of internal categories and descent along closed covers is standard in SGA4 Exp. Vbis (Saint-Donat/Deligne cohomological descent); not on this specific page form

ideas.what: Embedding X_{Δ*} ⊂ X × N(I), with simplicial operators acting on the I-flag factor
ideas.modern_name: Simplicial subspace of X × nerve(I); fibre over x is the nerve of I_x
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Čech/Mayer–Vietoris nerve of a closed cover)

deep.surprise_reason: This page is a routine, correct write-up of the nerve of an internal poset in Top. Grothendieck himself calls the construction 'de façon bien connue'. It is the standard simplicial replacement / homotopy colimit of a closed filtration, and nothing here goes beyond the known literature.
transcription_corrections: In (10), the first subscript is Δ_r (an overwritten character), so it reads X_{Δ_r}.
The last line of (10) reads ∐_{i_0 ∈ I} X_{i_0} × I_i(Δ_{r-1}); the subscript i presumably stands for i_0, i.e. I_{≥ i_0}.
In (11), the margin note reads 'ens. des drapeaux de longueur r de I', and the condition reads 'si i_* ∈ I(Δ_r)'.
